legend: Harry Potter is hiking in the Alps surrounding Lake Geneva. In this area there are m%%ZSMJ0%% cabins, numbered 1 to m%%ZSMJ1%%. Each cabin is connected, with one or more trails, to a central meeting point next to the lake. Each trail is either short or long. Cabin i%%ZSMJ2%% is connected with si%%ZSMJ3%% short trails and li%%ZSMJ4%% long trails to the lake.

Each day, Harry walks a trail from the cabin where he currently is to Lake Geneva, and then from there he walks a trail to any of the m%%ZSMJ5%% cabins (including the one he started in). However, as he has to finish the hike in a day, at least one of the two trails has to be short.
How many possible combinations of trails can Harry take if he starts in cabin 1 and walks for n%%ZSMJ6%% days?
input: The first line contains the integers m%%ZSMJ8%% and n%%ZSMJ9%%.
The second line contains m%%ZSMJ10%% integers, s1,…,sm%%ZSMJ11%%, where si%%ZSMJ12%% is the number of short trails between cabin i%%ZSMJ13%% and Lake Geneva.
The third and last line contains m%%ZSMJ14%% integers, l1,…,lm%%ZSMJ15%%, where li%%ZSMJ16%% is the number of long trails between cabin i%%ZSMJ17%% and Lake Geneva.
output: The number of possible combinations of trails, modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ21%%.
